retail_intro: Monday's crowd story is the Crypto Bowl, an industry buying America's biggest broadcast to recruit first-time buyers, a customer-acquisition binge WIRED likens to Pets.com [[n0112]], while invasion fears send hedgers into gold miners.

retail.title: Bitcoin / BTC — the Crypto Bowl recruitment drive
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The story the crowd tells itself is simple: when crypto is selling itself during the Super Bowl, the asset class has gone mainstream, and the only mistake is being late. Crypto companies are spending millions to win over viewers, CBS reported [[n0109]], and the New York Times told readers to prepare for this weekend's Crypto Bowl [[n0981]]. The Washington Post profiled a 29-year-old CEO pushing crypto during the Super Bowl by giving away millions in bitcoin [[n0916]], and Marketplace framed the game as the marriage of crypto and sports [[n0110]]. The hook is legitimacy by airtime plus free money. The price anchor flatters the pitch: bitcoin closed at 42,197.52 USD, up 15.12% over 20 sessions from 36,654.33 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-13).
What Is Driving It

The blitz is booked into a rebound that has already stalled: bitcoin and ether dipped as US inflation numbers dented the wider crypto market recovery again, Gadgets 360 reported [[n0958]]. Bitcoin slipped 0.11% on Sunday and is down 4.35% over five sessions, with ether off 7.66% to 2,883.46 USD and Solana 17.92% (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-13). The listed proxies took Friday's risk-off harder: Coinbase Global fell 5.00% to 194.53 USD and MicroStrategy 4.74% to 411.01 USD as the Nasdaq 100 lost 3.07% and the VIX jumped 14.43% to 27.36 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
The Social Signal

The attention evidence is about distribution more than chat-room volume. Terra signed a five-year, $40M sponsorship with the Washington Nationals [[n0942]]; Betterment is entering crypto through its Makara acquisition [[n1844]], which puts coins on a robo-adviser menu. The speculative fringe is warm as well: the Motley Fool is running if-you-had-invested-$100 stories on Shiba Inu [[n0951]], dogecoin added 3.15% on Sunday (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-13), a CryptoPunks NFT sold for nearly $24M, doubling the previous record [[n0964]], and Reese Witherspoon has been touting NFTs on Twitter [[n0983]]. When celebrities, ballparks and robo-advisers all point one way, the buyer being courted is the newcomer.
Historical Analog

WIRED's comparison is Pets.com [[n0112]], and the mechanism matters more than the brand: when an industry pours money into one mass-audience broadcast, it is admitting that its next leg of growth depends on people who have not bought yet. That is late-cycle customer acquisition, and it works only while prices reward the first purchase: a newcomer who buys after a 15.12% 20-session rebound and watches it fade becomes a seller, not a recruiter. Yahoo Finance's revival of the weird correlation between the Super Bowl and the stock market [[n1199]] treats the game itself as the signal. The ad slate is the better one, because heavy marketing at a peak of attention measures confidence among sellers, not durable demand among buyers.
Smart Money View

The professional split is real. Value investor Bill Miller says bitcoin miners are trading at very attractive valuations [[n0937]], Michael Saylor lays out why bitcoin beats property as a store of value [[n0889]], and Reuters reports Intel has launched a blockchain chip to tap the crypto boom [[n0789]]. Against that, the plumbing looks fragile: Coinbase removed cryptocurrency links after rug-pull warnings [[n0947]], and another $10M was lost in a DeFi hack of Binance-listed Dego Finance [[n0946]]. Regulators are circling the collectibles end of the pitch too: The Art Newspaper reports a US Treasury study finding the NFT market vulnerable to money laundering [[n0928]].
When the Narrative Breaks

The first test is conversion: airtime that does not turn into new accounts leaves the ad blitz looking like an acquisition bill paid near a local high. Price is the cleaner signal: a slide back toward the 20-session reference of 36,654.33 USD would erase the entire rebound the commercials are selling, and ether, already 7.66% lower over five sessions, is the faster warning (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-13). Macro supplies the trigger: the 10-year Treasury yield topped 2% for the first time since 2019 after the hot inflation print [[n2192]] before closing at 1.92% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11); a second break above 2% would reprice every liquidity-fed asset at once, and crypto has no earnings to cushion it. War is the calendar risk: the Biden–Putin call yielded no breakthrough, Al Jazeera reported [[n1494]], and weekend headlines hit crypto first because it is the only market open.

retail.title: Gold Miners ETF / GDX — the invasion hedge with leverage
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The war hedge is the most intuitive trade on the board: if Washington is pulling people out, own what rises on fear, with operating leverage. Biden told US citizens to leave Ukraine [[n1439]], the US ordered most embassy staff out [[n1496]], and gold jumped as rising Ukraine tensions spurred safe-haven demand [[n2209]]. Gold futures closed at 1,842.10 USD/oz, up 0.26%, but the miners did the shouting: GDX rose 5.67% to 32.43 USD and Northrop Grumman 4.53% to 399.32 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). The weekend added fuel, not relief: Biden told Putin an invasion would bring a decisive response, Reuters reported [[n1487]], and the talks yielded no breakthrough [[n1494]].
Where It Breaks

Miners amplify a headline premium and give it back fastest if diplomacy buys time; The Economist reports that a beleaguered Olaf Scholz has launched a diplomatic offensive [[n1335]], and any opening for talks would drain the bid. The underlying move is thin: gold is up 1.14% over 20 sessions from 1,821.40 USD/oz, and the 10Y Treasury yield at 1.92% is the hurdle a non-yielding hedge must beat (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11; US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11). A GDX close back below 31.24 USD, its 20-session reference, would mark the war premium as spent (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

retail.title: AMC Entertainment / AMC — the apes rally while Nasdaq bleeds
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The meme faithful are telling themselves their oldest story: when the market panics, the squeeze stocks are where the shorts get punished. AMC rose 22.54% over five sessions to 18.81 USD and GameStop 21.41% to 124.25 USD, and both gained on Friday while the Nasdaq 100 fell 3.07% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). AMC keeps feeding the believers, hiring a former Frito-Lay executive into a new growth role starting with popcorn [[n0496]], while the New York Times asks whether activist short sellers are misunderstood [[n0842]], a reminder the enemy is still there.
Where It Breaks

The rally lacks its old engine: Robinhood Markets fell 12.25% over five sessions to 13.32 USD while AMC and GameStop rose (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11), and WIRED says the app's psych experiment backfired horribly [[n0785]]. A squeeze needs new buyers through that door. AMC is still 8.95% below its 20-session reference of 20.66 USD; fading before reclaiming it would mark a relief pop, not a new leg.

retail.title: Affirm / AFRM — the buy-now darling loses a fifth
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Affirm is the purest buy-the-dip test on the board. The stock fell 20.67% on Friday to 46.55 USD, 25.82% over five sessions and 35.46% over 20 sessions from 72.13 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11), after results that PYMNTS says shine a light on merchant take-rate tradeoffs [[n0754]]. The bull case is Modern Retail's read that revenue growth is being driven by Amazon and Shopify [[n0755]]. MarketWatch's question about 15 pandemic stocks that rose 100% or more and have since been crushed, asking whether it is now time to buy [[n0861]], is exactly the itch being scratched.
Where It Breaks

Affirm lends into a bear-flattening curve, with the 2Y yield up 59 bps over 20 observations to 1.50% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11), which tends to raise funding costs for a lender. Banking Day says the Zebit exit highlights the challenges for a profitless BNPL sector [[n0731]], and peers offer no cover: PayPal is down 36.31% over 20 sessions and Upstart fell 5.64% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). New lows below 46.55 USD would turn the dip into a de-rating; the bull case needs stable take rates, not just a cheaper price.
